newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Belgrade bourse turnover falls in week to July 18.
newsitem.headline: Belgrade bourse turnover falls in week to July 18.

text.p: The Belgrade Stock Exchange (BSE) on Monday reported a 4.84 percent drop in turnover in the week ending July 18, with its short-term debentures index rising to 238.29 from the previous week's 192.02.
Total turnover in 103 transactions fell to 102.749 million dinars ($17.37 million) from 108.038 million dinars in the same number of deals a week ago.
The BSE short-term debentures index mirrors conditions under which companies and banks borrow and repay their debt.
It is calculated on volume, interest rate and maturity of the most bourse-traded short-term commercial papers and treasury bills. Index base is 1996.
* Commercial paper traded in 79 transactions for a volume of 16.742 million dinars.
* Treasury bills accounted 767,000 dinars in eight deals.
Interest rates on commercial paper and treasury bills ranged from 6.0 to 12.0 percent per month with maturity between seven and 60 days.
* There were five transactions in National Bank of Yugoslavia short-term bonds worth 45.0 million dinars.
* The Yugoslav government sold 39.55 million dinars worth of its 200-million-dinars of 30-, 60- and 90-day T-bills launched on July 10 to finance the federal budget.
On July 14, the remaining 15.85 million dinars of the first 50-million dinars tranche T-bills with 30-day maturity and a 3.5 percent monthly interest were sold.
In the week ending July 18, 23.70 million dinars of the second tranche of T-bills with 60-day maturity and 3.5 percent monthly interest were sold.
* Certificates of deposit traded in two deals worth 370,000 dinars.
* Shares accounted for 320,000 dinars and were traded in four deals.
* Over-the-counter trade in commercial paper and treasury bills rose to 60.274 million dinars from the previous week's 59.277 million.
* OTC trade in giro money, with banks trading their surplus liquidity, increased to 38.50 million dinars from 32.95 million a week earlier. -- Amra Kevic, Belgrade newsroom + 381 11 311 4305
